summary: Panama's investor residence routes are well documented in law: all decrees creating and changing the Qualified Investor Program (DE 722/2020, DE 109/2022, DE 193/2024, DE 17/2026), the Friendly Nations decrees (DE 416/2012, DE 197 and 226/2021) and the 2008 'Solvencia Económica Propia' rules were read in the Gaceta Oficial. Numbers are weaker: the Migration Service publishes yearly permit counts by category (approved/denied, 2010 to Aug 2026) but never by nationality within a category, and MICI's figures on certificates and investment come only from press releases, with inconsistent periods and units.

programs.name: Panama Qualified Investor Program (Residente Permanente en calidad de Inversionista Calificado)
programs.notes: Direct permanent residence (no provisional stage) for a qualifying investment from foreign funds, held for five years. Two steps: MICI (Dirección Nacional de Promoción de la Inversión) issues an investment certificate, then the SNM grants the permit (30 working days by decree). Created by Decreto Ejecutivo 722 of 15 Oct 2020 (Gaceta 29136, 16 Oct 2020); amended by DE 109 of 2022 and DE 193 of 2024; replaced ('subrogado') by DE 17 of 8 Sept 2026 (Gaceta 30613, 16 Sept 2026). Routes: real estate (incl. presale contracts), securities via the Panama stock exchange, fixed-term bank deposit. Citizenship: DE 17 art. 14 says holders and dependants may apply for naturalisation after five consecutive years of residence, under the Constitution. Applications can be filed from abroad through a lawyer.

programs.name: Panama Friendly Nations residence (Residente Permanente en calidad de nacionales de países específicos que mantienen relaciones amistosas, profesionales, económicas y de inversión; 'Países Amigos')
programs.notes: Residence for nationals of a closed list of countries (24 in 2012, about 50 by 2021). First created by DE 343 of 16 May 2012 (not seen; known from its repeal), replaced by DE 416 of 13 June 2012 (Gaceta 27058-A). Until 2021 it needed only an economic or professional activity and a modest bank balance, not an investment. From 7 Aug 2021 (DE 197 and DE 226 of 2021) applicants get a two-year provisional permit and must show either a job with a work permit, real estate worth at least B/.200,000, or a B/.200,000 three-year fixed deposit; permanent residence follows after two years. Not an investment programme in the strict sense: the SNM statistics count all Friendly Nations permits, whatever the route. Naturalisation rules are the general constitutional ones (not checked in this pass).

programs.name: Panama permanent residence for own economic solvency (Residente Permanente por Solvencia Económica Propia)
programs.notes: Older investor residence under the 2008 migration regulation (DE 320 of 8 Aug 2008, arts. 191-195): B/.300,000 of foreign funds in real estate, a three-year fixed deposit, or a mix of both. SNM statistics show it as a provisional permit followed by a permanent one. A similar 'Solvencia Propia' status existed before 2008 under Decreto Ley 16 of 1960 (the SNM series from 2010 includes it). DE 722 of 2020 and DE 17 of 2026 let pending or current Solvencia holders switch to the Qualified Investor route. Amendments after 2008 were not checked.

programs.name: Panama residence as investor in a large business (Inversionista de Macro-empresa)
programs.notes: Residence for foreigners who are sole holders of shares worth at least B/.160,000 in a company with a commercial licence (DE 320 of 2008, arts. 185-186). SNM approvals fell to 10-15 a year by 2020-2021; the category no longer appears separately in the 2022-2026 tables. Current status not checked.

gaps: No official statistics by nationality for any investor route. SNM country tables cover all residence permits combined; MICI gives only a top-five list of certificates (Aug 2025) with no stated period.

No regular MICI statistics: certificate and investment figures exist only in press releases and speeches, with shifting periods (calendar year, July-June, since inception), units (investors vs certificates) and currencies (B/., dólares, '$'). They conflict: 120 vs 132 new investors in H2 2024; cumulative investment 148 million (Jan 2025) vs 309.8 million (Dec 2025); 100 million vs more than 90.1 million for roughly July 2024-June/July 2025.

MICI certificate counts and SNM permit approvals do not match (e.g. 2024: about 187 investors certified vs 327 qualified-investor permit applications approved by SNM). Whether SNM counts include dependants, and whether MICI counts include annual re-certifications, is not stated.
SNM's 2010-2021 table has no 'Inversionista Calificado' row, so approvals for Oct 2020-2021 are missing (probably inside 'Otras').
No data on dependants, revocations or cancellations under the Qualified Investor Program, or on naturalisations of former investors.
Investment by route in money terms (as opposed to share of certificates) is not published.
Amendments after 2008 to the Solvencia Económica Propia amounts (and the Macro-empresa route) were not traced; the 2008 terms are recorded without an end date.
The Constitution's naturalisation article and the naturalisation law were not stored; the citizenship path is documented only via art. 14 of DE 17/2026.
Decreto Ejecutivo 343 of 16 May 2012 (first Friendly Nations decree) was not found; known only from its repeal in DE 416.
No IMF, FATF/GAFILAT, EU or parliamentary document examining the Qualified Investor Program was found in this pass; web search quota ran out early, so international sources were not searched.
